bagrat-iii-of-georgia.s: Bagrat III of the Bagrationi dynasty was the first king of a united Georgia. Heir through his mother to the Kingdom of Abkhazia and adopted by his kinsman David III of Tao, he became King of Abkhazia in 978 and inherited the lands of the Iberian Bagratids on his father's death…

bhopal-agency.s: The Bhopal Agency was a political agency within the Central India Agency of British India, supervising Bhopal State and a group of smaller states in western Malwa, among them Rajgarh, Narsinghgarh, Kurwai, Basoda, Pathari and Mohammadgarh. A British political agent based at…

battle-of-fei-river.s: The Battle of Fei River was fought in 383 in present-day Anhui, where a much smaller Eastern Jin army under Xie Xuan, directed by Xie An, routed the invading force of Fu Jian of the Former Qin. The defeat shattered Fu Jian's empire, which had unified northern China: subject…

bach-dang-river.s: The Bạch Đằng River is a tidal river in northern Vietnam near Hạ Long Bay. It was the site of three famous Vietnamese victories: Ngô Quyền's defeat of the Southern Han fleet in 938, which ended a millennium of Chinese rule, Lê Hoàn's defeat of the Song in 981, and Trần Hưng…

balsa-ii.s: Balša II was a lord of Zeta of the Balšić family, which took control of the land around Lake Skadar after Stefan Dušan's death. He ruled Zeta from 1378 and expanded into Albania, gaining Valona by marriage and seizing Durrës in 1385.

battle-of-lade.s: The Battle of Lade was a naval battle fought in 494 BCE off the island of Lade near Miletus. A Persian fleet, largely Phoenician, defeated the combined fleet of the Ionian Greek cities after the Samians and others deserted.

bernardo-ohiggins.s: Bernardo O'Higgins was a leader of Chilean independence and the son of an Irish-born viceroy of Peru. With José de San Martín and the Army of the Andes he defeated the royalists at Chacabuco in 1817 and Maipú in 1818.

black-forest.s: The Black Forest is a wooded mountain range in south-western Germany, between the upper Rhine valley and the sources of the Danube. In the Middle Ages its valleys were divided among the Zähringen, the margraves of Baden, the Fürstenberg, abbeys such as Saint Blasien and small…

brian-boru.s: Brian Boru was King of Munster from the Dál Cais dynasty and High King of Ireland from 1002. He broke the power of the Viking towns and of the Eóganachta, then forced the other provincial kings to accept his overlordship.

bogota.s: Bogotá, founded as Santa Fe de Bogotá by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada in 1538 on the high plain of the Muisca, became the capital of the Spanish New Kingdom of Granada. From the 18th century it was the seat of the Viceroyalty of New Granada, and after independence it became the…

battle-of-white-mountain.s: The Battle of White Mountain was fought near Prague on 8 November 1620, early in the Thirty Years' War. Imperial and Catholic League troops defeated the army of the Bohemian Estates and their elected king, Frederick V of the Palatinate.

ba-maw.s: Ba Maw was a Burmese lawyer and politician who served as the first premier of British Burma from 1937 to 1939. During the Japanese occupation he became head of the Japanese-sponsored State of Burma, declared independent in 1943.

badr-al-din-lulu.s: Badr al-Din Lu'lu' was a freed slave of the Zengid rulers of Mosul who became regent for their young heirs and, from 1234, ruler of Mosul in his own name. He governed for about forty years, patronising metalwork and architecture, and submitted to the Mongols.

bahr-al-ghazal.s: Bahr al-Ghazal is a region of north-western South Sudan named after the river that drains it into the White Nile. In the 19th century it was a centre of the ivory and slave trade, dominated by armed trading companies such as that of al-Zubayr Rahma Mansur, and became a…

baldwin-ii-of-jerusalem.s: Baldwin II, Baldwin of Bourcq, was Count of Edessa from 1100 and King of Jerusalem from 1118 to 1131. As count he was captured by the Turks at Harran in 1104 and held for several years.

baldwin-ii-of-constantinople.s: Baldwin II was the last Latin Emperor of Constantinople, from 1228. His shrinking empire was almost bankrupt, and he travelled the West seeking help, selling relics such as the Crown of Thorns to Louis IX of France and pawning his son to Venetian merchants.

banza-bakwai.s: The Banza Bakwai, the 'seven bastards', were the Hausa and neighbouring kingdoms that Hausa tradition regarded as less legitimate than the seven true Hausa states descended from Bayajidda. They usually include Zamfara, Kebbi, Yauri, Gwari, Nupe, Kwararafa and Yoruba.

baton-rouge.s: Baton Rouge is a city on the Mississippi River and the capital of the US state of Louisiana. A French post in the 18th century, it passed to Britain in 1763 as part of West Florida and to Spain in 1779.

benito-juarez.s: Benito Juárez was a Zapotec lawyer who served as President of Mexico from 1858 until his death in 1872. A leader of the liberal Reform, he separated church and state and defended the 1857 constitution in the Reform War.

black-hills.s: The Black Hills are a mountain range in South Dakota and Wyoming, sacred to the Lakota. The Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868 guaranteed them to the Great Sioux Reservation, but after gold was found during Custer's expedition of 1874 the United States seized them in 1877.

black-sea-fleet.s: The Black Sea Fleet is the Russian navy's fleet in the Black Sea, founded in 1783 after the annexation of Crimea and based at Sevastopol. In the revolution of 1917–1918 its sailors were a radical Bolshevik force that helped overrun Crimea.

black-volta.s: The Black Volta, or Mouhoun, is a river of West Africa that rises in western Burkina Faso, forms part of the borders of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, and joins the White Volta in Ghana to form the Volta. Trade routes linking the gold and kola forests to the Niger crossed it, and…

bogislaw-xiv.s: Bogislaw XIV was the last Duke of Pomerania of the House of Griffins, ruling Stettin from 1620 and all Pomerania from 1625. During the Thirty Years' War Sweden occupied the duchy from 1630.

bolko-ii-of-ziebice.s: Bolko II was a Silesian Piast duke who received Ziębice (Münsterberg) when his father Bolko I's lands were divided in 1322, founding it as a separate duchy. He became a vassal of King John of Bohemia in 1336, like most Silesian dukes, and was succeeded by his son Nicholas the…

bolko-ii-the-small.s: Bolko II the Small was Duke of Świdnica from 1326 and also of Jawor from 1346, the last independent Piast duke in Silesia. He refused Bohemian overlordship and allied with Poland.

bora-bora.s: Bora Bora is a volcanic island with a lagoon and barrier reef in the Leeward group of the Society Islands, in French Polynesia. In the 19th century it was ruled by its own chiefs and kings, rivals of Raiatea and Tahiti.

buba-yero.s: Buba Yero was a Fulani scholar and warrior who received a flag from Usman dan Fodio and founded the emirate of Gombe in north-east Nigeria in the early 19th century. Campaigning against Bornu, the Jukun and local peoples, he extended Sokoto's jihad into the Gongola and Benue…

battle-of-moira.s: The Battle of Moira, Mag Rath in Irish, was fought in 637 near Moira in County Down. The high king Domnall mac Áedo of the Northern Uí Néill defeated Congal Cáech, king of the Dál nAraidi, and his ally Domnall Brecc of Dál Riata; Congal was killed.

bulgarian-round-table.s: The Bulgarian Round Table was a series of talks in early 1990 between the Bulgarian Communist Party, newly renamed the Socialist Party, and the opposition Union of Democratic Forces. Held after Todor Zhivkov's fall in November 1989, they agreed on multi-party elections to a…

baba-beg.s: Baba Beg was one of the beks of the Kenagas Uzbek tribe who ruled the oasis of Shahrisabz in the mid-19th century, together with Jura Beg. They resisted the Manghit emirs of Bukhara and kept Shahrisabz effectively independent.

bae-jung-son.s: Bae Jung-son was a Goryeo military officer who led the Sambyeolcho units in revolt in 1270, when the court returned to Kaegyong and accepted Mongol overlordship. The rebels proclaimed the royal kinsman Wang On as king and sailed to Jindo island, where they built the Yongjang…

bahadur-shah-of-gujarat.s: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat was sultan of Gujarat from 1526 to 1537. He conquered Malwa and sacked Chittor, but was defeated by the Mughal emperor Humayun in 1535.

bahadur-shah-of-nepal.s: Bahadur Shah of Nepal was a son of Prithvi Narayan Shah and regent of the Kingdom of Nepal from 1785 to 1794 for his young nephew Rana Bahadur Shah. Under his leadership the Gorkha armies continued the unification of Nepal, annexing many hill kingdoms to the west, including…

baise-rajya.s: Baise Rajya, the 'twenty-two kingdoms', were the small hill principalities of the Karnali basin in western Nepal that emerged after the Khasa Malla kingdom broke up in the late 14th century. Jumla was the leading state, and Doti one of the largest.

baldwin-i-of-jerusalem.s: Baldwin I of Jerusalem, earlier known as Baldwin of Boulogne, was a leader of the First Crusade. In 1098 he left the main army and became ruler of Edessa, founding the first crusader state.

baldwin-i-of-flanders.s: Baldwin I of Flanders, called Iron Arm, was the first count of Flanders. In 862 he eloped with Judith, daughter of the West Frankish king Charles the Bald, who after reconciliation gave him lands around Bruges to defend against Viking raids.

baldwin-i-of-constantinople.s: Baldwin I, Latin Emperor, was count of Flanders and Hainaut and a leader of the Fourth Crusade. After the crusaders took Constantinople in 1204 he was elected the first emperor of the Latin Empire.

baldwin-of-alna.s: Baldwin of Alna was a Cistercian monk sent by the pope as legate to Livonia around 1230. He tried to bring the newly conquered Baltic lands under direct papal authority rather than the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, making treaties with Curonian leaders who accepted baptism.

balsa-iii.s: Balša III was the last lord of Zeta from the Balšić family, ruling the coast and hinterland of modern Montenegro and northern Albania from 1403. He fought long wars with Venice over Scutari and the coastal towns.

bani-utbah.s: The Bani Utbah were a confederation of Arab clans from central Arabia that migrated to the Gulf coast in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. Under the protection of the Banu Khalid they settled at Kuwait, where the Al Sabah became rulers, and at Zubarah in Qatar, from…

bani-yas.s: The Bani Yas are a tribal confederation of the south-eastern Gulf coast, originally based in the Liwa oases. Their leading Al Nahyan family founded Abu Dhabi in the 18th century, and in 1833 the Al Bu Falasah section moved to Dubai under the Al Maktoum.

banu-hilal.s: The Banu Hilal were an Arab tribal confederation from Arabia who migrated through Egypt to North Africa in the 11th century, encouraged by the Fatimids to punish the Zirids for breaking with Cairo. From the 1050s they defeated the Zirids, ravaged Ifriqiya and pushed the…

barrak-ibn-ghurayr.s: Barrak ibn Ghurayr was chief of the Banu Khalid, the leading tribal confederation of eastern Arabia. In 1670 he expelled the Ottoman garrison from al-Hasa and founded the Banu Khalid Emirate, with its centre at Hofuf.

bartolome-mitre.s: Bartolomé Mitre was an Argentine general, historian and statesman. As a leader of the State of Buenos Aires he defeated the Argentine Confederation at Pavón in 1861 and reunited the country, serving as president from 1862 to 1868.

bashar-al-assad.s: Bashar al-Assad was president of Syria from 2000, succeeding his father Hafez al-Assad. His violent repression of the protests of 2011 led to a civil war that killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions, in which he survived with Russian and Iranian help.

bashir-shihab-ii.s: Bashir Shihab II was emir of Mount Lebanon from 1789 to 1840, the most powerful ruler of the Shihab dynasty. Born a Muslim, he became a Maronite Christian and broke the power of rival Druze lords.

basic-law-for-the-federal-republic-of-ge.n: Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany
basic-law-for-the-federal-republic-of-ge.s: The Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany is the German constitution, drafted by a parliamentary council of the western states and in force from 23 May 1949. Intended as provisional until reunification, it set up a federal parliamentary democracy with strong basic…

battle-of-halani.s: The Battle of Halani was fought in Sindh in 1783 between the Talpur Baloch, led by Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur, and the last Kalhora ruler, Abdul Nabi. The Talpurs had turned against the Kalhoras after the murder of their leaders.

battle-of-muizenberg.s: The Battle of Muizenberg was fought near Cape Town from August to September 1795, when a British expedition attacked the Dutch Cape Colony to keep the sea route to India from France after the Netherlands fell to the French Republic. After weeks of skirmishing and the arrival…

battle-of-worringen.s: The Battle of Worringen was fought on 5 June 1288 near Cologne in the War of the Limburg Succession. Duke John I of Brabant, supported by the counts of Berg and Mark and by the citizens of Cologne, defeated Archbishop Siegfried of Westerburg and his allies, capturing the…

batu-khan.s: Batu Khan was a grandson of Genghis Khan and founder of the Golden Horde. He led the Mongol western campaign of 1236 to 1242, conquering the Volga Bulgars and the principalities of Rus' and invading Poland and Hungary.

bay-of-all-saints.s: The Bay of All Saints is a large bay on the coast of Bahia in north-eastern Brazil, named by Portuguese navigators in 1501. Salvador, founded on its shore in 1549, was the capital of colonial Brazil until 1763.

bay-of-kotor.s: The Bay of Kotor is a winding, fjord-like bay on the Adriatic coast of Montenegro, surrounded by steep limestone mountains. Its towns, such as Kotor and Perast, were held by Venice from 1420 to 1797 and were famous for seafaring.

bay-of-naples.s: The Bay of Naples is a gulf on the coast of Campania in southern Italy, overlooked by Mount Vesuvius and closed by the Sorrento peninsula and the islands of Ischia and Capri. Greek colonists settled its shores from the 8th century BCE, founding Cumae and Neapolis, and it later…

beaver-wars.s: The Beaver Wars were a long series of conflicts in which the Iroquois Confederacy, armed through Dutch and then English trade, fought neighbouring peoples and the French for control of the fur trade and for captives. In the mid-17th century the Iroquois destroyed or scattered…

bela-iv-of-hungary.s: Béla IV of Hungary was king from 1235 to 1270. The Mongols crushed his army at Mohi in 1241 and devastated Hungary, forcing him to flee to the Adriatic.

benedict-of-aniane.s: Benedict of Aniane was a Visigothic noble turned monk who founded the abbey of Aniane in southern France and became the chief monastic reformer of the Carolingian Empire. Under Louis the Pious, first in Aquitaine and then as emperor, he imposed the Rule of Saint Benedict on…

benjamin-franklin.s: Benjamin Franklin was a Philadelphia printer, writer, scientist and statesman. He founded a library, a fire company and the academy that became the University of Pennsylvania, and became famous for his experiments with electricity.

bento-goncalves.s: Bento Gonçalves was a rancher and soldier of Rio Grande do Sul who led the Ragamuffin War, or Farroupilha, against the Empire of Brazil from 1835. He was elected president of the breakaway Riograndense Republic, though he spent part of the war as a prisoner.

berengar-ii-of-italy.s: Berengar II of Italy was margrave of Ivrea who seized the Italian crown with his son Adalbert in 950. His imprisonment of Queen Adelaide brought the German king Otto I into Italy, and in 952 Berengar had to accept Otto as overlord and cede the marches of Verona and Friuli.

berengar-i-of-italy.s: Berengar I of Italy, margrave of Friuli and a grandson of Louis the Pious through his mother, was elected King of Italy when the Carolingian Empire broke up in 888. For decades he fought rival claimants such as Guy of Spoleto, Louis of Provence and Rudolf of Burgundy, while…

bernhard-iii-margrave-of-baden-baden.s: Bernhard III, Margrave of Baden-Baden, was a son of Margrave Christopher I of Baden. In 1535 he and his brother Ernest divided the Margraviate of Baden: Bernhard took the middle Rhine lands around Baden-Baden with a share of Sponheim, while Ernest received the lands later…

bernhard-iii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen.s: Bernhard III, Duke of Saxe-Meiningen, was the last reigning duke of Saxe-Meiningen, succeeding his father George II in 1914. A Prussian general and a scholar of ancient Greece, he was married to Princess Charlotte of Prussia, sister of Wilhelm II.

bhopawar-agency.s: Bhopawar Agency was a political agency of the British Central India Agency covering the hilly, largely Bhil country of south-western Malwa. A British political agent supervised its princely states, including Jhabua, Alirajpur, Barwani and many minor chiefships such as…

birnin-kebbi.s: Birnin Kebbi is a town in north-western Nigeria, a capital of the Hausa Kingdom of Kebbi from the 16th century. Its walls protected the kingdom founded by Muhammadu Kanta, but in 1805 it fell to the Fulani jihad of Usman dan Fodio, and Kebbi's rulers continued their resistance…

birnin-zamfara.s: Birnin Zamfara was the walled capital of the Hausa Kingdom of Zamfara in north-western Nigeria. From there Zamfara raided widely in the 17th century and controlled routes between Hausaland and the Niger.

biswa-singha.s: Biswa Singha was the founder of the Koch kingdom in the Brahmaputra valley and northern Bengal in the early 16th century. Uniting Koch chiefs after the fall of the Kamata kingdom, he made his capital at Kamatapur and promoted Hinduism, inviting Brahmins to his court.

blue-nile.s: The Blue Nile is the river that flows from Lake Tana in the Ethiopian highlands through a deep gorge into Sudan, joining the White Nile at Khartoum. It carries most of the Nile's floodwater and silt.

bogislaw-iv-duke-of-pomerania.s: Bogislaw IV, Duke of Pomerania, was a member of the Griffin dynasty. In 1295 he and his half-brother Otto I divided the Duchy of Pomerania: Bogislaw took the coastal lands north of the Peene and the east, ruling from Wolgast, while Otto received the lands around Stettin.

boleslaw-ii-the-bald.s: Bolesław II the Bald was a Silesian Piast duke, eldest son of Henry II the Pious, who was killed by the Mongols near Legnica in 1241. Quarrelsome and violent, he lost Silesia to divisions with his brothers and in 1248 kept the Duchy of Legnica.

boleslaw-iii-wrymouth.s: Bolesław III Wrymouth was duke of Poland from 1102 to 1138. He conquered Pomerania, defended Poland against the German emperor Henry V in 1109 and promoted the Christianisation of the Pomeranians.

brantas-river.s: The Brantas River is the longest river in East Java, flowing in a great arc around the Kelud and Arjuno volcanoes to the sea at Surabaya. Its fertile valley was the heartland of East Javanese kingdoms from the 10th century, including Kahuripan, Kediri, Singhasari and Majapahit.

british-columbia.s: British Columbia is the westernmost province of Canada, between the Rocky Mountains and the Pacific. Created as a British colony on the mainland in 1858 during the Fraser River gold rush, it was merged with the Colony of Vancouver Island in 1866.

british-north-borneo-company.s: The British North Borneo Company was a chartered company that governed North Borneo, modern Sabah, from 1881 to 1946 under a British royal charter. It held lands acquired from the sultans of Brunei and Sulu, ruled through a governor at Sandakan and developed tobacco and rubber…

buenaventura-baez.s: Buenaventura Báez was a Dominican politician who served five times as president between 1849 and 1878. With Pedro Santana he dominated the first Dominican republic, and later led the Red party in the second.

bukhar-khudah.s: Bukhar Khudah, 'lord of Bukhara', was the title of the local rulers of Bukhara before and during the Arab conquest of Transoxiana. The dynasty minted coins and ruled the Zarafshan delta from Varakhsha.

buyuk-suleyman-pasha.s: Büyük Süleyman Pasha, 'Sulayman the Great', was a Georgian-born mamluk who governed Baghdad for the Ottomans from 1780 to 1802, the high point of Mamluk Iraq. He restored order, enlarged the slave-soldier household and fought Persian incursions, Arab tribes and Wahhabi raiders.

battle-of-the-catalaunian-plains.s: The Battle of the Catalaunian Plains was fought in 451 in north-eastern Gaul between the Hunnic army of Attila and a coalition led by the Roman general Aetius and the Visigothic king Theodoric I. Theodoric was killed, but Attila withdrew from Gaul.

bundesrat-german-empire.s: The Bundesrat, or Federal Council, was the chamber representing the governments of the member states of the North German Confederation from 1867 and of the German Empire from 1871. Prussia held the most votes and the chancellor presided.

battle-on-the-ice.s: The Battle on the Ice was fought on 5 April 1242 on frozen Lake Peipus between the forces of the Novgorod Republic under Prince Alexander Nevsky and an army of the Livonian Order and the Bishopric of Dorpat. The crusaders were defeated, which checked their expansion into…

battle-of-mons-graupius.s: The Battle of Mons Graupius was fought in 83 or 84 CE in north-eastern Scotland between a Roman army under Gnaeus Julius Agricola and the Caledonians, whose leader Tacitus names as Calgacus. Tacitus records a decisive Roman victory, but the site of the battle is unknown.

babemba-traore.s: Babemba Traoré was the last king of Kénédougou, ruling from Sikasso in present-day Mali from 1893. He succeeded his brother Tieba, who had allied with the French, but refused French demands to accept a garrison.

babrak-karmal.s: Babrak Karmal was an Afghan communist politician and leader of the Parcham faction of the People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan. He was installed in power by the Soviet invasion of December 1979, which killed Hafizullah Amin, and led the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan…

bacons-rebellion.s: Bacon's Rebellion was an armed uprising in the Colony of Virginia in 1676, led by the planter Nathaniel Bacon against Governor William Berkeley. Frontier settlers, angered by the governor's refusal to wage war on Native peoples after raids linked to the displaced…

badan-singh.s: Badan Singh was a Jat chief who founded the ruling house of Bharatpur in northern India. Recognised as leader of the Jats around 1722 with the backing of Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber, he united the Jat clans of the Mathura and Agra region and built forts at Deeg and other…

badr-ibn-hasanwayh.s: Badr ibn Hasanwayh was the most prominent ruler of the Kurdish Hasanwayhid dynasty in the central Zagros, governing from 979 to 1014 under nominal Buyid overlordship. The Abbasid caliph gave him the title Nasir al-Dawla.

baetan-mac-cairill.s: Báetán mac Cairill was a king of the Dál Fiatach and over-king of the Ulaid in north-eastern Ireland who died in 581. Later Irish tradition presents him as one of the most powerful kings of his age, claiming authority over the Isle of Man and parts of Scotland.

baghdad-pact.s: The Baghdad Pact was a Cold War defensive alliance formed in 1955 by Iraq, Turkey, Iran, Pakistan and the United Kingdom, with the United States closely associated. It aimed to contain Soviet influence in the Middle East.

baghelkhand-agency.s: The Baghelkhand Agency was a political agency of British India within the Central India Agency, created in 1871. A British political agent supervised the princely states of the Baghelkhand region, led by Rewa, together with smaller states such as Maihar and Sohawal.

bahadur-shah-faruqi.s: Bahadur Shah Faruqi was the last sultan of Khandesh in the northern Deccan. When he refused to submit to the Mughal emperor Akbar, Mughal armies besieged his great fortress of Asirgarh, which surrendered in January 1601.

baja-california.s: Baja California is the long peninsula of north-western Mexico between the Pacific Ocean and the Gulf of California. Jesuit missionaries began Spanish settlement at Loreto in 1697, and the territory was administered as a province of New Spain, separated from Alta California in…

bajlaj-chan-kawiil.s: B'ajlaj Chan K'awiil was the first ruler of the Maya city of Dos Pilas in Guatemala, a member of Tikal's royal family installed there around 648. After defeat by the Kaan dynasty of Calakmul he became its ally and waged war against Tikal, winning a major victory over its king…

bakht-buland-shah.s: Bakht Buland Shah was a Gond king of Deogarh in central India in the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. He served in the army of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, converted to Islam and encouraged Hindu and Muslim settlers to clear and farm land.

bakht-singh-of-ajaigarh.s: Bakht Singh of Ajaigarh was a Bundela Rajput ruler descended from the house of Panna. After the British took Banda, the former seat of his family's branch, he was granted the hill fort of Ajaigarh and its lands by sanad in the early nineteenth century.

bakhtawar-singh-of-alwar.s: Bakhtawar Singh of Alwar was the second ruler of the Naruka Rajput state of Alwar in Rajasthan. During the Second Anglo-Maratha War he allied with the British against the Marathas, and in 1803 signed a treaty that brought Alwar under British protection.

balaram-deva.s: Balaram Deva was a prince of the Chauhan ruling family of Patna State in western Odisha who, according to tradition, founded a separate kingdom at Sambalpur on the middle Mahanadi. His kingdom soon became the leading power among the hill states of the region, known as the…

baldwin-of-ibelin.s: Baldwin of Ibelin was a baron of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, lord of Ramla and Mirabel and a son of Barisan of Ibelin. He fought in the Christian victory over Saladin at Montgisard in 1177.

balian-of-arsuf.s: Balian of Arsuf was a thirteenth-century baron of the Kingdom of Jerusalem from the Ibelin family, son of John of Ibelin, lord of Arsuf. He served as bailli, or regent, of the kingdom.

balian-of-ibelin.s: Balian of Ibelin was a leading baron of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the youngest son of Barisan of Ibelin. In 1177 he married the dowager queen Maria Komnene, gaining Nablus.

balkan-mountains.s: The Balkan Mountains are a range running about 550 kilometres east to west across Bulgaria into eastern Serbia, known in antiquity as the Haemus. Their passes, such as the Shipka Pass, controlled routes between the Danube plain and Thrace, making them a frontier and defensive…

baltic-way.s: The Baltic Way was a peaceful demonstration on 23 August 1989 in which about two million people joined hands in a human chain some 675 kilometres long across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Held on the fiftieth anniversary of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, it protested the Soviet…

baltit-fort.s: Baltit Fort is a fortified palace above Karimabad in the Hunza valley of northern Pakistan, with parts traditionally dated to the thirteenth century. For centuries it was the residence of the Mirs of Hunza, who controlled the Karakoram route towards Kashgar.

balwant-singh-of-benares.s: Balwant Singh of Benares was the son of Mansa Ram, a Bhumihar landholder who obtained the zamindari of Benares under the Nawab of Awadh. He turned the family's holdings into a semi-independent principality and built Ramnagar Fort on the Ganges opposite Varanasi.

ban-chao.s: Ban Chao was a general of the Eastern Han dynasty who brought the city-states of the Tarim Basin back under Chinese control. From the 70s CE he used Shule (Kashgar) as a base, subduing kingdoms such as Karasahr in 94, and served as Protector General of the Western Regions from…

buon-ma-thuot.s: Buôn Ma Thuột, known in the colonial period as Ban Me Thuot, is the main city of the Central Highlands of Vietnam. Under French rule it was the administrative centre of the highland Crown Domain, the Hoàng triều cương thổ, and of the coffee and rubber plantations of Đắk Lắk.

banda-aceh.s: Banda Aceh is a port city at the northern tip of Sumatra, Indonesia, near the entrance to the Strait of Malacca. As the capital of the Aceh Sultanate from the sixteenth century it dominated the pepper trade, and under Dutch rule after 1874 it was called Kutaraja.

banu-gomez.s: The Banu Gómez were a powerful noble family of the Kingdom of León, counts of Saldaña, Carrión and Liébana on the upper Carrión river. Descended from Count Diego Muñoz, they often rebelled against the Leonese kings and at times allied with Almanzor of Córdoba in the late tenth…

banu-kab.s: The Banu Ka'b are an Arab tribe of Khuzestan in south-western Iran who rose to power in the eighteenth century around Fallahiyeh, now Shadegan. As Safavid authority collapsed they built a sheikhdom with a river fleet on the Shatt al-Arab, challenging Persian and Ottoman forces.

banu-wazir.s: The Banu Wazir were a Muslim family of western al-Andalus who rose to power when Almoravid rule broke down in the 1140s. Led by Sidray ibn Wazir, they ruled Beja and Évora in present-day Portugal, and in 1145 members of the family took control of Badajoz, forming one of the…

baraq-hajib.s: Baraq Hajib was a Qara Khitai officer who had served the Khwarazmian Empire and founded the Qutlugh-Khanid dynasty of Kerman in southern Iran. During the chaos of the Mongol invasions he seized Kerman in 1222.

barchuq-art-tegin.s: Barchuq Art Tegin was the idiqut, or ruler, of the Uyghur Kingdom of Qocho in the Turfan region. In 1209 he threw off the overlordship of the Qara Khitai, killing their resident official, and submitted voluntarily to Genghis Khan.

barebones-parliament.s: Barebone's Parliament was an assembly of 140 members nominated by Oliver Cromwell and the army officers, which sat from July to December 1653 after the expulsion of the Rump Parliament. It took its name from the London member Praise-God Barebone.

barha-tegin.s: Barha Tegin is named by the eleventh-century scholar al-Biruni as the founder of the Turk Shahi dynasty, which replaced the Nezak rulers of Kabul and Kapisa around 665. Al-Biruni recorded traditions of a line of some sixty kings descended from him.

barisan-of-ibelin.s: Barisan of Ibelin was the founder of the Ibelin family, one of the most powerful noble houses of the crusader states. A knight who served as constable of Jaffa, he received the new castle of Ibelin from King Fulk around 1141.

barisone-ii-of-arborea.s: Barisone II of Arborea was judge, or ruler, of the Judicate of Arborea in western Sardinia from 1146. With money borrowed from Genoa he had himself crowned King of Sardinia by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa at Pavia in 1164, aiming to rule the whole island.

barthelemy-boganda.s: Barthélemy Boganda was the first Catholic priest from Ubangi-Shari and the leading nationalist politician of French Equatorial Africa. Elected to the French National Assembly in 1946, he founded the Movement for the Social Evolution of Black Africa and in December 1958…

bartolomeu-bueno-da-silva.s: Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva was a Paulista bandeirante, son of the explorer of the same name known as Anhanguera. In 1722 he led an expedition from São Paulo into the central plateau of Brazil and in 1725 found gold along the Vermelho river.

basdeo-panday.s: Basdeo Panday was a Trinidadian trade unionist and politician who led the sugar workers' union and founded the United National Congress. In 1995 he became prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago, the first of Indian descent, and served until 2001.

basil-boioannes.s: Basil Boioannes was the Byzantine catepan, or governor, of Italy from 1017 to 1027. In 1018 he crushed the rebellion of Melus of Bari and his Norman mercenaries at the second Battle of Cannae.

batan-grande.s: Batán Grande is an archaeological complex in the La Leche valley of Lambayeque on the north coast of Peru, now within the Pómac Forest sanctuary. It was the religious capital of the Middle Sicán culture around 900 to 1100, with monumental adobe platform mounds such as Huaca Loro.

batang-hari-river.s: The Batang Hari is the longest river of Sumatra, flowing about 800 kilometres from the Minangkabau highlands past Jambi to the Strait of Malacca. In the first millennium it carried gold and forest products to the coast and was the home of the Melayu kingdom and the temple…

bato-the-breucian.s: Bato the Breucian was a leader of the Breuci, a Pannonian people of the Sava valley, in the Great Illyrian Revolt against Rome that began in 6 CE. Together with Pinnes he joined forces with Bato of the Daesitiates.

battle-of-blaauwberg.s: The Battle of Blaauwberg was fought on 8 January 1806 near Cape Town, when a British force under General David Baird defeated the Batavian garrison of Governor Jan Willem Janssens. The Cape surrendered days later, beginning permanent British rule over the colony, which the…

battle-of-bornhoved.s: The Battle of Bornhöved was fought on 22 July 1227 in Holstein, where an alliance of north German princes, including Count Adolf IV of Holstein, Count Henry of Schwerin, the Archbishop of Bremen and the city of Lübeck, defeated King Valdemar II of Denmark. The victory ended…

battle-of-didgori.s: The Battle of Didgori was fought on 12 August 1121 west of Tbilisi, where King David IV the Builder of Georgia defeated a large Seljuk-led Muslim coalition. The victory allowed David to capture Tbilisi in 1122, ending the Emirate of Tbilisi and making the city his capital.

battle-of-hafrsfjord.s: The Battle of Hafrsfjord was a naval battle in the fjord near present-day Stavanger in Rogaland, traditionally dated around 872 but possibly later. According to the sagas, Harald Fairhair defeated an alliance of western Norwegian kings there.

battle-of-lindanise.s: The Battle of Lindanise was fought on 15 June 1219 at the site of present-day Tallinn, when the crusading army of King Valdemar II of Denmark defeated the Estonians of Rävala. The Danes then built a castle on Toompea, around which the town of Reval grew.

battle-of-mantinea-418-bce.s: The Battle of Mantinea of 418 BCE was the largest land battle of the Peloponnesian War, fought in Arcadia. A Spartan army under King Agis II defeated an alliance of Argos, Mantinea and Athens that had been formed to challenge Spartan dominance in the Peloponnese.

battle-of-nuuanu.s: The Battle of Nuʻuanu was fought on Oʻahu in May 1795, when Kamehameha I, armed with Western guns and advisers, defeated Kalanikūpule, ruler of Oʻahu and Maui. Many defenders were driven over the cliffs of the Nuʻuanu Pali.

battle-of-shela.s: The Battle of Shela was fought around 1812 or 1813 on the beach at Shela on Lamu Island, off the coast of present-day Kenya. The people of Lamu defeated a combined force from Pate and the Mazrui rulers of Mombasa.

battle-of-st-matthews-day.s: The Battle of St Matthew's Day was fought on 21 September 1217 near Viljandi in southern Estonia during the Livonian Crusade. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword and their Liv and Latgalian allies defeated an Estonian army.

battus-ii-of-cyrene.s: Battus II, called the Fortunate, was the third king of the Greek colony of Cyrene in Libya. He invited many new settlers from Greece, causing conflict with the native Libyans over land.

bawa-jan-gwarzo.s: Bawa Jan Gwarzo was sarkin, or king, of the Hausa state of Gobir in present-day northern Nigeria and Niger. A Muslim ruler who tolerated older religious practices, he invited the Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio to his court and granted concessions to his community.

bayanchur-khan.s: Bayanchur Khan was the second khagan of the Uyghur Khaganate, ruling from 747 to 759. He consolidated Uyghur rule over the Mongolian steppe and built the walled capital Ordu-Baliq on the Orkhon River.

bayeux-tapestry.s: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered cloth about 70 metres long depicting the events leading to the Norman conquest of England, ending with the Battle of Hastings in 1066. It was probably made in England in the 1070s for Bishop Odo of Bayeux and long hung in Bayeux Cathedral.

baz-bahadur.s: Baz Bahadur was the last sultan of Malwa, ruling from Mandu in central India. More devoted to music than to war, he is remembered for his romance with the singer Rupmati, celebrated in later poetry and painting.

baz-bahadur-chand.s: Baz Bahadur Chand was a raja of the Chand dynasty of Kumaon in the central Himalaya and a contemporary of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. He extended the kingdom northwards to the Tibetan border and campaigned against neighbouring Garhwal.

burebista.s: Burebista was a king of the Getae and Dacians who, from about 82 BCE, united their tribes into a powerful kingdom, aided by the high priest Deceneus. He extended his realm from the middle Danube to the Black Sea, defeating the Boii and Scordisci and sacking Greek cities such…

bechara-el-khoury.s: Bechara El Khoury was a Maronite lawyer and politician who became the first president of independent Lebanon, serving from 1943 to 1952. With the Sunni leader Riad Al Solh he agreed the unwritten National Pact of 1943, which shared the main offices of state among religious…

bedir-khan-beg.s: Bedir Khan Beg was the last mir of the Kurdish Emirate of Bohtan, ruling from Cizre. In the 1840s he extended his power across the region, and his forces massacred Assyrian Christians of Hakkari in 1843 and 1846.

belarmino-tomas.s: Belarmino Tomás was a Spanish Socialist miners' leader from Asturias. During the Asturian revolution of October 1934 he negotiated the miners' surrender.

beleheb-kat.s: Beleheb' Kat was one of the two kings of the Kaqchikel Maya, ruling from Iximche in the Guatemalan highlands alongside Kaji' Imox. In 1524 the two kings received Pedro de Alvarado as an ally against the K'iche', and Iximche briefly became the first Spanish capital in Guatemala.

beleheb-tzi.s: Beleheb Tz'i was one of the leading kings of the K'iche' Maya kingdom in highland Guatemala at the time of the Spanish conquest. After defeating the K'iche' near Quetzaltenango in 1524, Pedro de Alvarado accused Beleheb Tz'i and Oxib Keh of plotting against him and had them…

belek-ghazi.s: Belek Ghazi was an Artuqid Turkoman emir, a nephew of Ilghazi, who held Harput and other fortresses in eastern Anatolia. In 1122 he captured Joscelin I of the County of Edessa and in 1123 King Baldwin II of Jerusalem, holding them at Harput, though Joscelin escaped.

belize-city.s: Belize City is the largest city of Belize, at the mouth of the Belize River on the Caribbean coast. It grew from a settlement of British logwood and mahogany cutters, the Baymen, and served as capital of British Honduras.

belovezha-accords.s: The Belovezha Accords were signed on 8 December 1991 at Viskuli in the Belovezha Forest of Belarus by the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus: Boris Yeltsin, Leonid Kravchuk and Stanislav Shushkevich. They declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and founded the…

benazir-bhutto.s: Benazir Bhutto was a Pakistani politician, daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and leader of the Pakistan Peoples Party. She served as prime minister from 1988 to 1990 and from 1993 to 1996, the first woman to lead the government of a Muslim-majority country.

benedetto-carushomo.s: Benedetto Carushomo was a leader of the medieval Commune of Rome who, in the early 1190s, took power as sole senator in place of the many senators of the commune. He ruled the city and its territory largely independently of the pope for about two years.

benedetto-zaccaria.s: Benedetto Zaccaria was a Genoese admiral, diplomat and merchant. In 1275 the Byzantine emperor Michael VIII granted him and his brother Manuel the alum mines of Phocaea, which made the family dominant in the European alum trade.

benjamin-hornigold.s: Benjamin Hornigold was an English pirate based at Nassau in the Bahamas, one of the founders of the pirate community known as the Republic of Pirates. Edward Teach, later called Blackbeard, served under him.

benjamin-kallay.s: Benjamin Kállay was a Hungarian statesman and historian who served as joint finance minister of Austria-Hungary from 1882 to 1903, in charge of the administration of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He promoted a shared Bosnian identity to counter Serbian and Croatian nationalism and…

benno-of-meissen.s: Benno of Meissen was Bishop of Meissen from 1066 and a supporter of the papacy against Emperor Henry IV during the Investiture Controversy. He was canonised in 1523, a ceremony that Martin Luther attacked in a pamphlet.

beqaa-valley.s: The Beqaa Valley is a fertile high plain in eastern Lebanon between the Mount Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges, drained by the Litani and Orontes rivers. In antiquity it held Chalcis and the temple city of Heliopolis, now Baalbek, and was the base of Ituraean and Herodian princes.

berenice-ii.s: Berenice II was the daughter of Magas, king of Cyrene, and queen of Ptolemaic Egypt. Promised to Ptolemy III, she was instead married to Demetrius the Fair, whom she had killed.

berleburg-castle.s: Berleburg Castle is a palace in Bad Berleburg in the Wittgenstein region of Westphalia, Germany. It was the residence of the counts, later princes, of Sayn-Wittgenstein-Berleburg, who rebuilt the medieval castle into a Baroque palace in the eighteenth century.

berlin-conference.s: The Berlin Conference was a meeting of European powers and the United States convened by Otto von Bismarck from November 1884 to February 1885. It set rules for European claims in Africa, required effective occupation of coastal territory and recognised King Leopold II's Congo…

berlin-wall.s: The Berlin Wall was a guarded barrier built by the German Democratic Republic from 13 August 1961 to cut off West Berlin and stop East Germans fleeing to the West. It became the leading symbol of the Cold War division of Europe.

bernabe-araoz.s: Bernabé Aráoz was an Argentine caudillo from Tucumán who supported the patriot army in the war of independence, notably at the Battle of Tucumán in 1812. As governor of Tucumán, he proclaimed the Republic of Tucumán in 1820 after the collapse of central government in the…

bernard-ato-iv-trencavel.s: Bernard Ato IV was a member of the Trencavel family and viscount of Carcassonne, Béziers, Albi, Nîmes and Razès in Languedoc. Inheriting Carcassonne through his mother Ermengard, he built a principality between the rival counts of Toulouse and Barcelona, balancing between them.

bernard-de-neufmarche.s: Bernard de Neufmarché was a Norman lord of the Welsh borders who conquered the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog in the late eleventh century. In 1093 his forces killed Rhys ap Tewdwr, king of Deheubarth, near Brecon.

bernard-of-septimania.s: Bernard of Septimania was a Frankish noble, son of William of Gellone, who held the counties of Barcelona and Septimania and led the defence of the Spanish March against the Umayyads. In 829 Louis the Pious made him chamberlain, and his influence at court helped provoke…

bernard-i-of-armagnac.s: Bernard I, called the Squinter, was the first count of Armagnac in Gascony, a member of the ruling house of the counts of Fezensac. Around 960 Armagnac was separated as his share of the family lands.

bernard-vi-of-armagnac.s: Bernard VI was count of Armagnac and Fezensac in south-western France. Through his marriage to Cécile, daughter and heiress of Count Henry II of Rodez, he gained the county of Rodez in 1302, which became one of the chief holdings of the house of Armagnac.

bernardo-de-galvez.s: Bernardo de Gálvez was a Spanish soldier who became governor of Spanish Louisiana in 1777. When Spain entered the American Revolutionary War, he used New Orleans as a base to capture British posts in West Florida, taking Baton Rouge in 1779, Mobile in 1780 and Pensacola in 1781.

bernard-i-duke-of-saxony.s: Bernard I was Duke of Saxony from 973 to 1011, the son of Hermann Billung. He continued his father's role as guardian of the Billung march against the Slavic peoples east of the Elbe, though the great Slavic revolt of 983 undermined German control there.

bernhard-i-duke-of-saxe-meiningen.s: Bernhard I was the first Duke of Saxe-Meiningen, third son of Ernest the Pious of Saxe-Gotha. In the 1680 partition of his father's lands he received Meiningen in the Werra valley, made the small town his residence and built Elisabethenburg Palace.

bernhard-ii-of-lippe.s: Bernhard II was lord of Lippe in Westphalia and a companion of Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony. Around 1185 he founded the town of Lippstadt, and he also founded Lemgo, laying the foundations of the later principality of Lippe.

bernhard-ii-duke-of-saxe-meiningen.s: Bernhard II was Duke of Saxe-Meiningen from 1803, under a regency until 1821, to 1866. During his reign the duchy gained additional territory in 1826 and its court culture grew.

bertrand-dogeron.s: Bertrand d'Ogeron was a French colonial governor appointed by the French West India Company in 1665 to govern Tortuga and the French settlements on the coast of Hispaniola. He encouraged buccaneers to settle as planters, brought settlers and women from France, and organised…

bertrand-of-baux.s: Bertrand of Baux was a Provençal lord of the house of Baux who acquired the principality of Orange through his marriage to Tiburge, heiress of the lords of Orange. Recognised as prince by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, he founded a line of Baux princes that ruled Orange for…

bettino-ricasoli.s: Bettino Ricasoli was a Tuscan baron and statesman who led the provisional government of Tuscany in 1859–1860, after the grand duke fled, and steered its union with the Kingdom of Sardinia. He succeeded Cavour as prime minister of the new Kingdom of Italy in 1861–1862 and…

bhagwan-rao-of-datia.s: Bhagwan Rao was a Bundela Rajput prince, son of Bir Singh Deo of Orchha, who received Datia in 1626 and founded it as a separate state. His father had already built the great seven-storey palace at Datia.

bhaskara-ravi-varman.s: Bhaskara Ravi Varman was a king of the Chera Perumals of Makotai, the dynasty that ruled much of Kerala from Mahodayapuram. He is best known for the Jewish copper plates, which granted a Jewish merchant, Joseph Rabban, trading privileges and the rights of a lord at Muziris.

bhava-naga.s: Bhava Naga was a king of the Naga dynasty of Padmavati in central India, whose line was known for Shaiva devotion and horse sacrifices. He married his daughter to Gautamiputra, son of the Vakataka king Pravarasena I, and his grandson Rudrasena I became a Vakataka king.

bhawani-singh-of-jhalawar.s: Bhawani Singh was Maharaj Rana of Jhalawar in Rajputana from 1899 to 1929. Known for his learning and interest in education, he founded schools and a library and built the Bhawani Natyashala theatre in Jhalawar.

bhawanrao-pant-pratinidhi.s: Bhawanrao Pant Pratinidhi was the Raja of Aundh, a small Maratha state near Satara, from 1909 to 1947. A painter and patron of the arts, he did much to popularise the surya namaskar exercise.

bhoja-ii-of-kolhapur.s: Bhoja II was the last major king of the Shilahara dynasty of Kolhapur in the western Deccan. As the power of the Western Chalukyas and Kalachuris collapsed in the late twelfth century, he ruled independently and took imperial titles.

bhupal-singh-of-udaipur.s: Bhupal Singh was Maharana of Udaipur, the ruler of Mewar, from 1930 until his death in 1955. Head of the senior Rajput house of Rajputana, he took Mewar into the Indian Union and in 1949 became Maharajpramukh of the United State of Rajasthan, a ceremonial head of state ranking…

bhupatindra-malla.s: Bhupatindra Malla was king of Bhaktapur, one of the three Newar kingdoms of the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal. A great builder, he raised the five-storey Nyatapola temple in 1702, the tallest pagoda in the valley, and enlarged the royal palace of fifty-five windows.

bhupinder-singh-of-patiala.s: Bhupinder Singh was Maharaja of Patiala, the leading Sikh princely state of the Punjab, from 1900 to 1938. Famous for his lavish lifestyle and jewels, including the Patiala Necklace made by Cartier, he was also a keen cricketer and patron who captained an Indian team in…

bhuvanaikabahu-iv.s: Bhuvanaikabahu IV was a Sinhalese king who moved the royal seat from Kurunegala to Gampola on the Mahaweli river around 1341. His reign saw the building of the Gadaladeniya and Lankatilaka temples, which blend Sinhalese, South Indian and other styles.

big-bear.s: Big Bear, Mistahimaskwa in Cree, was a Plains Cree chief who long refused to sign Treaty 6 with Canada, holding out for better terms until 1882 as the bison disappeared. During the North-West Rebellion of 1885 warriors of his band killed settlers at Frog Lake against his wishes.

bijjala-ii.s: Bijjala II was the most important ruler of the Kalachuris of Kalyani in the Deccan. A feudatory and minister of the Western Chalukya king Taila III, he seized the capital Kalyani around 1156 and proclaimed himself emperor by 1162.

bikram-singh-of-seraikela.s: Bikram Singh was the founder of Seraikela State on the Chota Nagpur plateau in present-day Jharkhand. A member of the Singh Deo ruling family of Porahat, he carved out his own principality on the Kharkai river around 1620.

bilge-kul-qadir-khan.s: Bilge Kul Qadir Khan was a Karluk leader in Central Asia who proclaimed himself khagan after the fall of the Uyghur Khaganate in 840. Many historians regard this as the founding of the Kara-Khanid Khanate, the first Turkic dynasty to adopt Islam as a state religion.

bimbisara.s: Bimbisara was king of Magadha in eastern India, ruling from Rajagriha, and a patron and contemporary of the Buddha. He expanded his kingdom by conquering Anga and through marriage alliances, including with a princess of Kosala whose dowry included revenue from a Kashi village.

binnya-dala.s: Binnya Dala was the last king of the Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom of the Mon in Lower Burma, ruling from Pegu from 1747. With French help he built up an army and in 1752 captured Ava, ending the Toungoo dynasty.

bir-chandra-manikya.s: Bir Chandra Manikya was Maharaja of Tripura from 1862 to 1896. He rebuilt Agartala as a modern capital and introduced administrative reforms on the British Indian model.

bir-sen.s: Bir Sen is the traditional founder of Suket State in the western Himalaya, said to have come from a Sen family of Bengal and to have established the kingdom around 765, with an early capital at Pangna. The rulers of Suket traced their descent from him, and Mandi State was…

birger-jarl.s: Birger Jarl was a Swedish statesman who held the office of jarl from 1248 and governed for his son King Valdemar, founding the Folkung dynasty. He strengthened royal law and authority, is traditionally credited with founding Stockholm around 1250, and led the crusade that…

bishopric-of-worms.s: The Bishopric of Worms was a diocese on the middle Rhine, centred on the cathedral city of Worms, whose bishops also ruled a small territory as princes of the Holy Roman Empire. In the High Middle Ages it held lands and rights that local lords such as the counts of…

bismarck-archipelago.s: The Bismarck Archipelago is a group of islands off north-eastern New Guinea, including New Britain, New Ireland and the Admiralty Islands. Germany annexed it in 1884 as part of German New Guinea, naming it after Otto von Bismarck.

black-loyalists.s: The Black Loyalists were people of African descent, many formerly enslaved, who sided with Britain in the American Revolutionary War in return for promises of freedom. About 3,000 were evacuated to Nova Scotia in 1783, settling at Birchtown and elsewhere, but faced poor land…

black-river-honduras.s: Black River was a British settlement at the mouth of a river on the Caribbean coast of Honduras, founded in the 1730s by settlers allied with the Miskito. From 1749 it was the headquarters of the British superintendent of the Mosquito Shore.

black-river-asia.s: The Black River, or Da River, rises in Yunnan in China and flows south-east through the mountains of north-western Vietnam to join the Red River. Its valley was home to Tai peoples organised in chiefly domains known as the Sip Song Chau Tai, the twelve Tai lands, from which…

blanca-alfonso-de-molina.s: Blanca Alfonso de Molina was Lady of Molina, daughter of the infante Alfonso de Molina and the heiress Mafalda. She ruled the lordship of Molina on the border of Castile and Aragon in the late 13th century.

battle-of-blood-river.s: The Battle of Blood River was fought on 16 December 1838 on the Ncome River in Natal between about 470 Voortrekkers under Andries Pretorius and a much larger army of King Dingane's Zulu. Defending a wagon laager with firearms, the Voortrekkers killed some 3,000 Zulu without…

blue-jacket.s: Blue Jacket was a Shawnee war leader in the Ohio country. With Little Turtle of the Miami he led the Western Confederacy of Native nations against American expansion, defeating Josiah Harmar in 1790 and Arthur St.

bogd-khan.s: The Bogd Khan was the 8th Jebtsundamba Khutuktu, the head of Tibetan Buddhism in Mongolia, born in Tibet. When Qing rule collapsed in 1911, Mongol nobles proclaimed him Great Khan of an independent Mongolia, ruling from Urga.

bogislaw-x.s: Bogislaw X was Duke of Pomerania from 1474, called the Great. By 1478 he had reunited all the divided Pomeranian duchies under his rule.

bogu-qaghan.s: Bögü Qaghan was ruler of the Uyghur Khaganate from 759 to 779. He helped the Tang dynasty against the rebels of the An Lushan revolt, and in 762 he adopted Manichaeism from Sogdian missionaries met at Luoyang, making it the state religion of the Uyghurs.

bohemond-vi-of-antioch.s: Bohemond VI was Prince of Antioch and Count of Tripoli from 1252. In 1260 he submitted to the Mongols under Hulagu and joined their advance into Syria, which brought papal excommunication and Mamluk hostility.

boleslaw-i-the-brave.s: Bolesław I the Brave was Duke of Poland from 992 and its first crowned king in 1025. Son of Mieszko I, he hosted Emperor Otto III at Gniezno in 1000, when an archbishopric was established there.

boleslaw-ii-of-masovia.s: Bolesław II of Masovia was a Piast duke who received Płock when the Duchy of Masovia was divided in 1275, and later reunited most of Masovia under his rule. He was briefly Duke of Kraków in 1288 and was married to a Lithuanian princess, which tied Masovia to its pagan neighbour.

boleslaw-iii-the-generous.s: Bolesław III the Generous was a Silesian Piast duke, son of Henry V of Legnica. In 1311 he took Brzeg on the Oder as his share of the inheritance, creating the Duchy of Brzeg, and he also held Legnica for a time.

boleslaw-the-elder-of-niemodlin.s: Bolesław the Elder was a Silesian Piast duke, a son of Bolko I of Opole. On his father's death in 1313 he received the castle town of Niemodlin, west of Opole, as a separate duchy.

boleslaw-v-the-chaste.s: Bolesław V the Chaste was Duke of Kraków and Sandomierz from 1243. His reign saw repeated Mongol invasions of Lesser Poland, in 1241 and 1259 to 1260.

bolko-i-the-strict.s: Bolko I the Strict was a Silesian Piast duke, son of Bolesław II the Bald. He received Jawor in 1274, added Świdnica around 1291 and built a strong duchy along the Bohemian border, guarded by castles such as Bolków and Grodziec.

bono-manso.s: Bono Manso was the capital of the Akan kingdom of Bono, near modern Techiman in central Ghana. It lay where the savanna meets the forest, close to gold-bearing lands, and grew as a market for Mande merchants trading gold and kola.

book-of-llandaff.s: The Book of Llandaff is a manuscript compiled at Llandaff Cathedral in south-east Wales around 1125. Written to support the claims of the bishops of Llandaff, it contains saints' lives and about 150 charters recording land grants.

boqor-osman-mahamuud.s: Boqor Osman Mahamuud was king of the Majeerteen Sultanate in north-eastern Somalia in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. He fought a long war with his kinsman Yusuf Ali Kenadid, who left to found the Sultanate of Hobyo.

boris-iii-of-bulgaria.s: Boris III was Tsar of Bulgaria from 1918, when his father Ferdinand abdicated after defeat in the First World War. From 1935 he ruled through a personal regime.

boris-yeltsin.s: Boris Yeltsin was a Soviet and Russian politician, elected President of the Russian SFSR in June 1991. He led resistance to the August 1991 coup attempt in Moscow and agreed the dissolution of the Soviet Union in December 1991.

borrell-ii-of-barcelona.s: Borrell II was Count of Barcelona, Girona and Osona from 947 and Count of Urgell from 948. He sought ties with the Caliphate of Córdoba and the papacy.

borso-deste.s: Borso d'Este was lord of Ferrara from 1450. Emperor Frederick III made him Duke of Modena and Reggio in 1452, and Pope Paul II made him Duke of Ferrara in 1471, shortly before his death.

bosnian-church.s: The Bosnian Church was an independent Christian church in medieval Bosnia, separate from both Rome and Constantinople and accused by Catholic writers of dualist heresy. Led by a bishop called the djed, it had the support of many nobles alongside Catholic and Orthodox communities.

boso-the-old.s: Boso the Old was a lord of Charroux in Poitou who held comital authority in La Marche, a frontier district of Aquitaine, around 958. He is regarded as the founder of the counts of La Marche, and his descendants ruled both La Marche and the neighbouring county of Périgord.

boyko-borisov.s: Boyko Borisov is a Bulgarian politician, a former chief secretary of the interior ministry and mayor of Sofia, who founded the centre-right GERB party. He served as prime minister three times between 2009 and 2021 and dominated Bulgarian politics until mass anti-corruption…

brabant-revolution.s: The Brabant Revolution was an uprising in the Austrian Netherlands against the centralising and church reforms of Emperor Joseph II. Beginning in Brabant in 1789, rebels drove out the Austrian forces and in January 1790 proclaimed the United Belgian States.

bracara-augusta.s: Bracara Augusta was a Roman city founded under Augustus around 16 BCE in north-western Hispania, on the site of modern Braga in Portugal. It became a centre of the Callaeci and, after the reforms of Diocletian, capital of the province of Gallaecia.

braccio-da-montone.s: Braccio da Montone was an Italian condottiere from Perugia, one of the most famous mercenary captains of his age. He seized Perugia in 1416 and ruled it as lord, also extending his power over much of Umbria and the Marche.

brahima-saydu.s: Brahima Saydu was a Fulbe leader who, inspired by the jihad of Usman dan Fodio, led the Fulbe of Liptako in a rising against their Gurma rulers around 1810. After defeating the Gurma he founded the Emirate of Liptako, with its capital at Dori in present-day Burkina Faso, under…

brahmanism.s: Brahmanism is the name given to the Vedic tradition of religion and social order maintained by Brahmin priests, centred on sacrifice, ritual purity, Sanskrit learning and the hierarchy of the varnas. In early medieval India kings such as the Varmans and Senas of Bengal…

brandub-mac-echach.s: Brandub mac Echach was a King of Leinster of the Uí Chennselaig. In 598 he defeated and killed the high king Áed mac Ainmuirech of the northern Uí Néill at the Battle of Dún Bolg, a victory long celebrated in Leinster tradition.

braulio-carrillo.s: Braulio Carrillo was head of state of Costa Rica from 1835 to 1837 and again from 1838 to 1842. He defeated the rival towns of Cartago, Heredia and Alajuela in the War of the League in 1835, fixed the capital at San José, encouraged coffee growing and reformed the law.

brazzaville-conference.s: The Brazzaville Conference was a meeting of Free French colonial officials opened by Charles de Gaulle at Brazzaville in January 1944. It recommended reforms in French Africa, including the end of forced labour and wider political representation, while rejecting…

brenner-pass.s: The Brenner Pass is a pass through the Alps between Innsbruck in Austria and Bolzano in Italy, one of the lowest major crossings of the main Alpine ridge. Since Roman times it has carried the route from Germany down the Adige valley into the Po plain, and emperors used it for…

brian-orourke.s: Sir Brian O'Rourke was lord of West Breifne in Connacht, in present-day County Leitrim. He resisted English authority, sheltered survivors of the Spanish Armada in 1588 and rose against the governor Richard Bingham.

bridei-son-of-beli.s: Bridei son of Beli was King of Fortriu and overking of the Picts from about 671. In 685 he destroyed the Northumbrian army and killed King Ecgfrith at the Battle of Dun Nechtain, ending English overlordship in northern Britain.

brigham-young.s: Brigham Young was the second president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, leading it from 1844. He organised the migration of the Mormons from Illinois to the Salt Lake Valley in 1847 and directed the settlement of much of the Great Basin.

british-isles.s: The British Isles are the group of islands off north-western Europe made up of Great Britain, Ireland and many smaller islands, including the Hebrides, Orkney and Shetland. From the late 8th century Norse raiders and settlers established colonies there, and many of the…

buluggin-ibn-ziri.s: Buluggin ibn Ziri was a Sanhaja Berber leader, son of Ziri ibn Manad, and the founder of the Zirid dynasty. When the Fatimid caliph al-Mu'izz moved to Egypt in 972, he made Buluggin governor of Ifriqiya.

buoso-da-dovara.s: Buoso da Dovara was a Ghibelline nobleman who dominated Cremona in the mid-13th century, at times jointly with Uberto Pallavicino. Entrusted with defending Lombardy against Charles of Anjou's army in 1265, he was accused of taking bribes to let it pass, and Dante placed him…

burchard-ii-duke-of-swabia.s: Burchard II was Duke of Swabia from 917. After King Conrad I executed the previous duke Erchanger, Burchard took control of Alamannia, defeated King Rudolf II of Upper Burgundy at Winterthur in 919 and was recognised by Henry the Fowler the same year.

burgundian-wars.s: The Burgundian Wars were fought between Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, and the Old Swiss Confederacy with its allies. The Swiss defeated him at Grandson and Murten in 1476, and he was killed at Nancy in 1477.

burhanuddin-rabbani.s: Burhanuddin Rabbani was an Afghan Islamic scholar and leader of the Jamiat-e Islami party. After the mujahideen took Kabul in 1992 he became President of the Islamic State of Afghanistan, but the government was torn by civil war and lost Kabul to the Taliban in 1996.

burna-buriash-ii.s: Burna-Buriash II was a Kassite king of Babylonia in the 14th century BCE. Several of his letters to the Egyptian pharaohs Akhenaten and Tutankhamun survive among the Amarna letters, in which he exchanged gifts, demanded gold and arranged royal marriages.

butuga-ii.s: Butuga II was a king of the Western Ganga dynasty of southern Karnataka. A son-in-law and ally of the Rashtrakuta emperor Krishna III, he fought for him against the Cholas and is credited with killing the Chola prince Rajaditya at the Battle of Takkolam in 949.

buurba-jolof.s: Buurba Jolof was the title of the kings of the Jolof Empire, who were overlords of the Wolof states of Senegal. In 1549 Amari Ngoone Sobel Fall of Cayor defeated and killed the Buurba at the Battle of Danki, after which Cayor, Baol, Walo and other coastal states broke away and…

buyruk-khan.s: Buyruk Khan was a son of the Naiman ruler Inanch Bilge Khan, who after his father's death in the 1190s ruled part of the Naiman khanate in the Altai mountains while his brother Tayang Khan ruled the rest. The brothers' rivalry weakened the Naiman against Temüjin, the future…

buzurg-khan.s: Buzurg Khan was a Khoja of the Afaqi line, descended from the former rulers of Kashgar, who lived in exile in Kokand. In 1865 rebels in Kashgar invited him to lead them against Qing rule, and he arrived with the general Yaqub Beg.

battle-of-canhe-slope.s: The Battle of Canhe Slope was fought in 395 in northern China between the Later Yan army of Murong Bao and the forces of Tuoba Gui of Northern Wei. The Wei surprised the retreating Yan army and destroyed it, killing or capturing tens of thousands.

battle-of-the-crocus-field.s: The Battle of the Crocus Field was fought in Thessaly in 352 BCE during the Third Sacred War. Philip II of Macedon, leading the Thessalian League, defeated the Phocians under Onomarchus, who was killed, and some 3,000 prisoners were drowned as temple robbers.

battle-of-ngoc-hoi-dong-da.s: The Battle of Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa was fought around Thăng Long (Hanoi) in early 1789, when Nguyen Hue, who had just proclaimed himself Emperor Quang Trung, launched a surprise Lunar New Year attack on a Qing army sent to restore the Later Le dynasty. The Qing forces were routed,…

bolko-i-of-opole.s: Bolko I of Opole was a Silesian duke of the Piast dynasty who ruled Opole from 1281. A supporter of the Czech kings, he extended his influence in Upper Silesia.

battle-of-dun-bolg.s: The Battle of Dún Bolg was fought in Leinster in 598, when Brandub mac Echach, king of Leinster and of the Uí Chennselaig, defeated the Uí Néill high king Áed mac Ainmuirech, who was killed. The victory checked Uí Néill attempts to dominate Leinster and made Brandub the most…

battle-of-dun-nechtain.s: The Battle of Dun Nechtain, or Nechtansmere, was fought on 20 May 685 between the Picts under Bridei son of Beli and the Northumbrians under King Ecgfrith, who was killed. The Pictish victory destroyed the Northumbrian army and ended English domination over the Picts and much…

blackbeard.s: Blackbeard, Edward Teach or Thatch, was an English pirate of the Caribbean and the American coast. Associated with the pirate base at Nassau, he captured a French slave ship in 1717, renamed it Queen Anne's Revenge and blockaded Charleston in 1718.

battle-of-ager-sanguinis.s: The Battle of Ager Sanguinis, the 'Field of Blood', was fought on 28 June 1119 near Sarmada, west of Aleppo. Ilghazi, the Artuqid ruler of Mardin and Aleppo, surrounded and destroyed the army of the Principality of Antioch, killing its regent Roger of Salerno.

behanzin.s: Béhanzin was the last independent king of Dahomey, reigning from 1889 to 1894. He fought two wars against France over its claims to the coast around Porto-Novo and Cotonou, but French forces under General Alfred-Amédée Dodds took Abomey in 1892.

battle-of-lake-regillus.s: The Battle of Lake Regillus was a legendary victory of the early Roman Republic over the Latin League, traditionally dated around 496 BCE, near Tusculum in the Alban Hills. The Latins were said to be led by Octavius Mamilius of Tusculum on behalf of the exiled Tarquinius…

battle-of-las-carreras.s: The Battle of Las Carreras was fought in April 1849 near Baní in the Dominican Republic, where Dominican forces under Pedro Santana defeated the invading Haitian army of President Faustin Soulouque. The victory checked Haiti's attempts to reconquer the eastern part of Hispaniola.

bakhtiyar-khalji.s: Bakhtiyar Khalji was a Turkic-Afghan commander of the Ghurids who conquered Bihar and western Bengal at the end of the 12th century. His raids in Bihar destroyed Buddhist monasteries such as Odantapuri, and around 1204 he surprised the Sena king Lakshmana Sena at Nadia.

boun-oum.s: Boun Oum was the hereditary prince of Champasak in southern Laos. In 1946 he renounced his dynastic claims so that Laos could be unified under the king of Luang Phrabang, and in return became inspector general of the kingdom.

battle-of-quatre-bras.s: The Battle of Quatre Bras was fought on 16 June 1815 at a crossroads south of Brussels, two days before Waterloo. Wellington's Anglo-allied army held off Marshal Ney's French corps, keeping the road open to join with the Prussians.

battle-of-red-cliffs.s: The Battle of Red Cliffs was fought on the Yangtze in the winter of 208–209, at the end of the Han dynasty. The allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei, led by Zhou Yu, defeated the much larger army of the northern warlord Cao Cao, partly through fire ships.

battle-of-sabana-larga.s: The Battle of Sabana Larga was fought on 24 January 1856 near Dajabón in the north-west of the Dominican Republic. Dominican forces defeated the army of the Haitian emperor Faustin Soulouque, ending his last attempt to reconquer the eastern part of Hispaniola.

battle-of-san-carlos-1872.s: The Battle of San Carlos was fought on 8 March 1872 near the fort of San Carlos, in present-day San Carlos de Bolívar, Buenos Aires Province. An Argentine army with allied indigenous warriors under Cipriano Catriel defeated the forces of the Mapuche leader Calfucurá.

battle-of-san-jacinto.s: The Battle of San Jacinto was fought on 21 April 1836 near present-day Houston and decided the Texas Revolution. Texan forces under Sam Houston surprised the Mexican army of Antonio López de Santa Anna, routing it in less than twenty minutes.

benjamin-durban.s: Sir Benjamin D'Urban was a British army officer and governor of the Cape Colony from 1834 to 1838. After the Sixth Xhosa War he annexed the land between the Keiskamma and Kei rivers in 1835 as the Province of Queen Adelaide, but the British government reversed the annexation…

brasidas.s: Brasidas was a Spartan general of the Peloponnesian War. In 424 BCE he marched through Thessaly to the Chalcidice, where he won over Athenian allies and captured Amphipolis.
